enqueue_job and claim_job run through NativeJobStore.run_operation. Enqueue requires resources cpu/memory_mib/gpu/model_calls as integers >= 0, capabilities stored sorted and unique, lease_seconds 1..3600, a work item and parent in the workspace, and, when trial_id is set, a proposed trial of that work on an admitted or running campaign. A cancelled parent or ancestor raises job_cancelled and writes no row. An identical job_id replays; any other row with that id is idempotency_conflict. The insert is source native, backlog, fence 0, plus an enqueued event. OMP-404-s05 adds an item-budget gate after the validations and before the insert, for the root item (the parent's chain top, or the work item itself): an exhausted usd/tokens/wall_clock dimension cancels the item tree and refuses, and a child that would take the tree past max_subagents cancels the tree and writes the subagents budget.exceeded alert first. A refusal returns {status refused, code budget_exceeded} from apply, and because a raise inside the transaction would roll back the alert and the stop, enqueue_job raises JobError budget_exceeded only after the transaction commits (replays included). After a child insert the same transaction calls check_item_budget, so a child that crosses a subagents threshold writes the 50 or 80 row at enqueue. claim_job reads only the workers row, locks it, and with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED considers the oldest backlog native job whose capabilities the worker holds, whose resource weight (sum of the four fields) fits capacity minus the weight of that worker's unreleased reservations, that fits caller-specified resource_limits (cpu/memory_mib/gpu/model_calls >= 0) against unreleased reservations plus the candidate job, and that has no cancelled ancestor; a candidate whose root item budget is exhausted returns job null instead of being leased. A trial job is leased only while the trial is proposed, the campaign is admitted or running, and the worker component is in compatibility.workers. The lease sets admitted, fence+1, attempt+1, worker_id, lease_expires_at, reservation {job_id}:{fence}, and a claimed event. An unknown or inactive worker is job_worker_unavailable; no match returns job null

OMP-404: item budget accounting, threshold alerts, and the budget-driven stop. item_budget reads the payload.draft.budget of the work item's newest intake_publication receipt (None when the receipt or its budget is absent). root_work_id walks the parent_job_id chain to its top work item, bounded against a self-parent cycle. item_spend sums price_usd and input+output tokens over the recursive CTE of the work item's jobs plus every parent_job_id descendant whichever work item it belongs to, plus the work item's job-less usage, and reports wall_clock_seconds as the age of the oldest tree job and subagents as the count of tree jobs with a parent. check_item_budget is a no-op for an unbudgeted item; otherwise it writes one committed budget_alert outbox row per reached threshold, keyed by sha256(workspace, work, dimension, threshold) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, carrying event budget.threshold_reached at 50 and 80 and budget.exceeded at 100, dimension, threshold_percent, spent, and limit. usd, tokens, and wall_clock_seconds alert at 50/80/100 and report the dimension exhausted once spend reaches the limit; subagents alerts at 50/80 by count/max only (silent when max is 0) and is never exhausted. OMP-404-s05: when any dimension is exhausted, check_item_budget also calls cancel_item_tree with reason budget_exceeded in the same transaction, so the alerts and the item-tree stopping commit together. sweep_item_budgets visits the workspace's source=native work items that carry an intake_publication receipt and have a non-terminal job, each in its own transaction, and returns the work ids whose tree check_item_budget stopped (work-clock enforcement with no usage row). alert_subagents_exceeded writes the subagents budget.exceeded row at the cap; the enqueue refusal path calls it, since check_item_budget never reports subagents exhausted

cancel_job runs through NativeJobStore.run_operation. It locks the target and every same-workspace descendant with a recursive CTE on parent_job_id, FOR UPDATE, ordered by job_id. Each native backlog or admitted job becomes cancelled with cancel_reason, cancelled_at, and updated_at; an admitted job also gains fence+1, loses worker_id, and has its open {job_id}:{fence} reservation released as cancelled, so the holder's renew and settle raise job_fence_stale. Sealed and failed jobs stay. One cancelled event is appended per job cancelled. The result is {status, job_ids}. A target already cancelled for the same reason replays and does not write the job, its events, or its reservation again; a different reason is idempotency_conflict. A missing target, or a sealed or failed target, is invalid_request and writes nothing. OMP-404-s05 adds cancel_item_tree, the item-scoped counterpart the budget stopper calls with the caller's open cursor: it validates the reason, locks the work item's own jobs plus every parent_job_id descendant (whichever work item), in job_id order FOR UPDATE, then cancels the native backlog and admitted rows through the same _cancel_rows rules. It is a sub-operation of the enclosing transaction, not run_operation, so it stamps the enclosing operation id and has no separate replay; sealed, failed, and already-cancelled jobs are left alone

OMP-404-s06: send_alert POSTs a JSON budget alert with Authorization Bearer and Idempotency-Key event_id using stdlib urllib, allows only https plus http to 127.0.0.1 or localhost, does not follow redirects or proxies, and raises GrokbotError on non-2xx or network errors without including the token. deliver_budget_alerts sends one workspace's committed or failed budget_alert outbox rows in event_id order under FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, re-commits a failed row with apply_commit, closes a sent row via recover_unacked_commit(evidence_trusted=True) and close, marks a delivery error failed via recover_unacked_commit(evidence_trusted=False) for retry, and returns the number sent

renew_lease, settle_job, and reconcile_jobs run through NativeJobStore.run_operation. Renew and settle hold only a native admitted job whose worker_id and fence match and whose lease_expires_at is still after now; otherwise job_fence_stale and nothing is written. renew_lease adds lease_seconds to the job lease and the unreleased {job_id}:{fence} reservation expiry. settle_job maps succeeded to sealed and failed to failed. Each receipt role is audit, release, or evaluator; its evidence must validate as an R02 evidence document of kind receipt, and its issuer must be a registered workspace component whose kind equals that role; otherwise invalid_request and nothing is written. Settlement {outcome, fence, worker_id, receipts} is written once with settled_at, the reservation is released as settled, and a settled event is appended. A terminal job replays a byte-identical settlement under a new operation id and keeps the stored receipts; any other settlement is job_fence_stale. reconcile_jobs returns each admitted native job with lease_expires_at at or before now to backlog with fence+1, null worker_id and lease_expires_at, releases that reservation as lease_expired, appends a lease_expired event, and returns {status, job_ids}; a second call returns no job ids

deliver_outbox drains one workspace's committed or failed usage_ledger omp_jobs.outbox rows to the usage ledger file; OMP-404 adds the kind='usage_ledger' filter so budget_alert rows written by jobs.budget have no file-ledger effect and stay untouched. Rows are read in event_id order under FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. A failed row is committed again first (apply_commit, revision+1). An event whose usage_id is already in the ledger closes without appending; otherwise the payload is appended with research_ledger.append_ledger_event and counted, and a raised append returns the row to failed via recover_unacked_commit(evidence_trusted=False) for retry. A present usage_id is acknowledged and closed via recover_unacked_commit(evidence_trusted=True) plus close. A crash between the append and the state update leaves the row committed, so the next call finds the usage_id and closes without appending: the external effect happens at most once. State changes reuse contracts/v1/recovery, adding no second state machine

trial_execution projects trial state from its latest root native job in omp_jobs into queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled; gating requires status succeeded, all trial jobs terminal (unsettled_jobs), and root settlement containing trusted audit and release receipts from issuers in the campaign compatibility manifest (missing_audit_receipt, missing_release_receipt, untrusted_receipt, issuer_not_in_manifest), adhering to R02 scientific success constraints

dispatch_trial enqueues the trial:<trial_id> native compute job with the research.trial capability on the work's proposed trial. factory builds the handler from worker options (harness_dir, work_url, bearer_file, workspace_id, default_timeout) and either calls an injected execute or constructs a WorkClient. run reads the trial and its campaign spec, resolves the trial's evaluator component descriptor, and loads the harness from harness_dir/<evaluator artifact_sha256>; a missing file or a bytes_sha256 mismatch fails the job with no observation and no run. The harness runs as a bash autoresearch.sh in a fresh temporary cwd with timeout campaign spec.resource_vector.max_wall_seconds else the default 600s, and its output is scanned for finite METRIC name=value lines, skipping __proto__, constructor, and prototype. The run is recorded through the WorkService as a legacy_autoresearch observation with observation_id uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, omp-job:<job_id>), source_ref job:<job_id>, the trial's campaign_id and trial_id, execution_status completed, crashed, or timed_out, payload {metrics, exit_code, duration_seconds, harness_sha256}, payload_sha256 v1.canonical.sha256 of that payload, and observed_at now. The job is settled succeeded only when the harness exits 0 within the timeout, with an evaluator receipt carrying the trial evaluator issuer, content_digest equal to payload_sha256 and trust verified; observe rebuilds the same settlement from the stored observation without running and run reuses it when one exists. python -m omp_work.jobs.research_trial check dispatches the job, ticks one worker, and prints {capability: autoresearch, passed, observation, receipt}

NativeJobStore over role omp_work_app with RLS context. run_operation replays the same operation_id and request only inside its workspace and raises idempotency_conflict for another workspace or a changed request. append_event writes only a native job in the caller's workspace. job_view/worker_view expose every row column. cancelled_ancestor walks to the nearest cancelled ancestor. register_worker and drain_worker hash workspace_id into the request; capabilities are sorted and confined to the registered R02 worker descriptor; identical re-register replays; a changed or draining worker is job_worker_unavailable; drain is permanent. project_trial maps backlog=queued, admitted=leased, sealed=succeeded, failed, cancelled, and reports a job-less trial (or an unmigrated jobs ledger) as queued and ineligible; a trial is eligible only when every native job is sealed with settlement and settled_at. record_usage writes omp_jobs.usage_events and research_ledger.append_ledger_event once per operation

record_usage runs through NativeJobStore.run_operation for WP5 accounting on omp_jobs.usage_events. Computes a stable usage_id from sha256(workspace_id, work_id, job_id, request_id). If job_id is provided, validates that the job exists in the workspace and matches work_id (job-less usage is permitted for preflight). An identical existing usage_id replays without writing or advancing step_index; any field discrepancy raises idempotency_conflict. A new row sets conversation_id to job_id or work_id, source_file to omp_jobs:native, step_index to 1 + max for that conversation/source_file, tokens to the sum of input/output/cache tokens only if all counts are known else NULL, and in the same transaction writes an outbox row with kind usage_ledger, CloseoutRecord committed state, revision 1, and the job_usage ledger event payload. OMP-404 appends to the same transaction one check_item_budget over the usage job's root_work_id (else the usage work_id): an item with no intake_publication budget writes nothing, a replay adds nothing, and each reached threshold writes its budget_alert outbox row
